title: Efficacy of Sunvozertinib in Heavily Pretreated Patients With EGFR-Mutated Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Real-World Study.
authors: Li X, Ding K, Song R et al.
abstract: IntroductionPatients with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) often develop resistance after multiple therapies, resulting in limited effective later-line treatment options. This study aimed to evaluate the real-world efficacy and safety of sunvozertinib in heavily pretreated patients with EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC.MethodsThis was a multicenter retrospective observational study. A total of 67 patients with advanced EGFR-mutated NSCLC from eight hospitals in Zhejiang Province between 2023 and 2025 were included. All patients had received at least two prior lines of therapy and were treated with sunvozertinib. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR), and secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), disease control rate (DCR), and safety.ResultsThe 67 patients (median age 62; 47.8% male) harbored EGFR exon 19 deletion (19del) (26.9%), L858R (34.3%), EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations (exon 20ins) (32.8%), or other mutations (6.0%). Median prior therapies were three. ORR was 32.8% with 22 partial responses, and DCR was 71.6%. Median PFS was 3.2 months (95% CI, 2.3-5.2), and median OS was 10.7 months (95% CI, 6.1-NA). Among patients with baseline brain metastases, the intracranial disease control rate (iDCR) was 73.1%. Most adverse events were grade 1-2 and manageable. The most common treatment-related adverse events were diarrhea (26.9%), fatigue (28.4%), rash (23.9%), paronychia (17.9%), and stomatitis (17.9%). Grade ≥3 adverse events were infrequent.ConclusionsSunvozertinib demonstrated real-world antitumor activity and manageable toxicity in heavily pretreated EGFR-mutated NSCLC, providing supportive, hypothesis-generating real-world evidence that warrants prospective confirmation.

title: Long-Term Recurrence-Free Survival After Surgery and Adjuvant Furmonertinib in a Patient With EGFR-Mutated Pulmonary Sarcomatoid Carcinoma: A Case Report.
authors: Nong M, Tan X
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma (PSC) is an extremely rare subtype of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), which generally shows limited response to chemoradiotherapy and confers poor overall survival (OS). Recent progress in molecular targeted therapy has provided potential therapeutic strategies for this disease. Herein, we report a rare case of PSC harboring concurrent EGFR L858R and PIK3CA exon 10 mutations. The patient underwent radical surgical resection followed by adjuvant third-generation epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI) targeted therapy, and sustained long-term disease-free survival (DFS) was observed during clinical follow-up. Although this case showed a favorable outcome, causality cannot be established from a single case report. Whether adjuvant furmonertinib contributed to the long-term DFS remains uncertain and requires further investigation.
CASE: A middle-aged female presented with cough, expectoration, and hemoptysis. Percutaneous lung biopsy confirmed Stage IIIA pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma, and radical surgical resection was subsequently performed. Postoperative next-generation sequencing identified concomitant EGFR L858R and PIK3CA exon 10 mutations. The patient received adjuvant furmonertinib as postoperative targeted therapy. No tumor recurrence was detected throughout follow-up, with a documented DFS of 48 months.
CONCLUSION: Surgical resection remains the primary treatment for patients with early-stage PSC, and postoperative molecular testing is critical to identify targetable mutations. This patient obtained durable DFS after radical resection combined with adjuvant third-generation EGFR-TKI targeted therapy. Additional large-scale studies are needed to confirm the efficacy of adjuvant EGFR-TKIs in PSC patients with dual EGFR/PIK3CA mutations.

title: Quinazoline derivatives with dual EGFR and VEGFR-2 inhibition: insights from docking, molecular dynamics, and in vivo studies.
authors: Yassen ASA, Nafie MS, Kishk SM et al.
abstract: Tumor growth, angiogenesis, and metastasis are influenced by EGFR and VEGFR-2; therefore, dual targeting of EGFR and VEGFR-2 is an attractive approach for cancer management. Here, novel quinazoline analogues 4-23 were designed and synthesized as dual EGFR and VEGFR-2 TK inhibitors. In vitro enzymatic inhibitory activities against EGFR and VEGFR-2 and cytotoxic activities against lung A549 and breast MCF-7 cancer cell lines were evaluated. Compound 18 had potent cytotoxicity against A549 cells with an IC50 value of 9.41 µM, compared with 9.43 µM for sorafenib. On the other hand, compound 15 had potent cytotoxicity against MCF-7 cells with an IC50 value of 5.08 µM, compared with 4.94 µM for sorafenib, and poor cytotoxicity against A549 cells. Compound 15 exhibited a remarkable dual EGFR and VEGFR-2 inhibitory activity with IC50 values of 0.04 and 0.086 µM, compared with sorafenib 0.035 and 0.09 µM, respectively, while compound 18 exhibited promising inhibitory activity against EGFR with an IC50 value of 0.07 µM and moderate activity against VEGFR-2. For apoptosis investigation, compound 15 significantly stimulated total apoptotic breast cancer cell death by 27.17-fold, arresting the cell proliferation at the G2/M-phase, while compound 18 significantly stimulated apoptotic lung cancer cell death by 7.95-fold. In vivo studies showed that compound 15 exhibited tumor inhibition by 72%, compared with 65% inhibition for the sorafenib-treated group. Finally, docking studies and molecular dynamic simulations were performed to explore the probable binding modes. Taken together, in vitro, in silico, and in vivo results revealed that compound 15 had high drug potential as a dual-target inhibitor of EGFR/VEGFR-2 to inhibit breast cancer growth and apoptosis.

title: Severe cutaneous adverse reaction to aumolertinib plus vebreltinib in an EGFR-mutant NSCLC patient: a case report.
authors: Zhang Y, Zhang L, Ding J
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The combination of aumolertinib and vebreltinib has emerged as an effective therapeutic strategy for advanced non-small cell lung cancer(NSCLC) harboring EGFR mutations with concurrent MET amplification. However, the safety profile of this combination regimen remains incompletely characterized, particularly with respect to severe cutaneous adverse reactions.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 72-year-old female patient with NSCLC harboring EGFR 19Del and MET amplification. Fifteen days after initiating treatment with the combination of aumolertinib and vebreltinib, the patient developed severe oral mucositis and rapidly progressive generalized exfoliative dermatitis, clinically suspected as Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS/TEN) or an SJS/TEN-like reaction. No skin biopsy was performed because the family declined; therefore, histopathological confirmation was unavailable. The patient was admitted on February 5, 2026. SCORTEN was calculated using the available admission parameters and was 4. Initial treatment with intravenous methylprednisolone (40mg QD) for three days was of limited efficacy; therefore, the dose was escalated to 60mg BID, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) and human albumin were added. Due to inadequate response after four days of high-dose corticosteroid therapy, a single dose of the TNF-α inhibitor adalimumab (80mg) was administered subcutaneously as a rescue therapy. The patient was transferred to a specialized dermatology hospital the following day. The patient was transferred to a specialized dermatology hospital the following day. Telephone follow-up indicated clinical improvement after continued adalimumab plus corticosteroids; she was discharged after four weeks. However, complete external records and discharge photographs were unavailable, and the effectiveness of adalimumab cannot be established from this case.
CONCLUSION: The combination of aumolertinib and vebreltinib has been associated with a rare but life-threatening suspected SJS/TEN-like reaction that can be refractory to conventional-dose corticosteroids. Adalimumab plus corticosteroids was administered as rescue therapy in this case, but its efficacy cannot be determined based on a single case and incomplete follow-up. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for this cutaneous toxicity, promptly discontinue suspected drugs, and arrange specialized care.

title: Co-alterations associated with resistance to EGFR inhibitors in advanced EGFR-positive NSCLC: insights from the precision oncology program in two large international real-world cohorts.
authors: Boos LA, Doerig C, Camarillo-Retamosa E et al.
abstract: EGFR inhibitors (EGFRi), alone or combined with chemotherapy or bispecific antibodies, are standard first-line therapy for advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC, but their efficacy is limited by heterogeneous resistance mechanisms. To define the impact of genetic co-alterations, we analyzed two complementary real-world cohorts. Patients with EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R mutations were included from the University Hospital Zurich (USZ; n = 43) and the Flatiron Health-Foundation Medicine clinicogenomic database (FH-FMI CGDB; n = 1927). Duration of treatment (DOT) on first-line EGFRi was assessed in relation to co-alterations at diagnosis. In the FH-FMI CGDB, shorter DOT on osimertinib was associated with co-alterations in ERBB2 (p < 0.01), PIK3CA (p = 0.04), and TP53 (p < 0.01), with similar trends for MET, KRAS, BRAF, and CCNE1. For erlotinib/afatinib, shorter DOT was observed for ERBB2 (p = 0.027) and TP53 (p < 0.01), alongside additional genes. The USZ cohort showed concordant trends. TP53 was the most frequent co-alteration; variants affecting zinc-binding and dimerization domains were associated with shorter DOT. These findings identify co-alterations linked to reduced EGFRi benefit, particularly ERBB2, PIK3CA, and TP53, and highlight residue-specific TP53 effects. This supports comprehensive genomic profiling and function-based stratification to refine treatment strategies in EGFR-mutant NSCLC.

title: Clinicogenomic determinants of early progression on first-line osimertinib in EGFR-mutant NSCLC.
authors: Pecci F, Jeng MY, Di Federico A et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: With the recent approvals of the FLAURA2 and MARIPOSA regimens in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), identifying clinico-genomic features predictive of suboptimal outcomes with first-line osimertinib monotherapy is critical in guiding upfront treatment selections.
METHODS: This is a multicenter retrospective study enrolling patients with advanced NSCLC harboring common EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletions [ex19del], L858R) treated with first-line osimertinib monotherapy across 13 centers (Clinical cohort). Comprehensive baseline genomic data on tumor tissue were available for DFCI and MSKCC (Genomic cohort). The association of clinicogenomic features with real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS) was investigated. Caris Life Science cohort was used for RNA-sequencing analysis.
RESULTS: A total of 1488 patients were enrolled in the clinical cohort; at median follow-up of 43.3 months, median rwPFS was 16.3 months (95%CI 15.3-17.4), median overall survival was 36.7 months (95%CI 34.8-39.4). TP53 mutated (TP53MUT) was independently associated with shorter rwPFS compared with TP53 wild-type (TP53WT), specifically in EGFR ex19del (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.68, p<0.001) than in L858R subgroup (aHR 1.18, p=0.2). Using a survROC model for rwPFS, PD-L1 was the variable with greatest impact on risk of progression at 6 (ΔAUC=0.0549) and 12 (ΔAUC=0.0348) months. In the genomic cohort, patients with TSGMUT (RBM10, CREBBP, ATM, RB1, KMT2D, TSC2, PTEN) had shorted rwPFS compared to TSGWT (aHR 1.5, p=0.01), specifically in L858R subgroup (aHR 1.8, p=0.02). Combining TP53 with TSG, pts with TP53MUT plus at least one TSGMUT and pts with TP53WT-TSGMUT had shorter rwPFS compared to TP53WT-TSGWT and TP53MUT-TSGWT. In the genomic cohort, PD-L1 TPS was the strongest predictor of very-early rwPFS (ΔAUC=0.16), followed by TP53-TSG (ΔAUC=0.08). PD-L1 was associated with higher MET mRNA and immunohistochemistry expression and transcriptional program enriched for proliferative, inflammatory, and metabolic signaling pathways.
CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter real-world cohort, baseline PD-L1 and TP53 combined with TSG predict very-early progression to first-line osimertinib, with EGFR subtype-specific prognostic impact of genomic co-alterations.

title: Phase 1b/2 to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, and Efficacy of TXN10128 in Combination With TOPO-I Inhibitor-based Therapies (Irinotecan or TROP2 ADC) in Advanced or Metastatic EGFR Mutated NSCLC
summary:
This is a multicenter, open-label, multi-cohort, Phase 1b/2 clinical study. This study evaluates TXN10128 in combination with either irinotecan (a topoisomerase I inhibitor) or a TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate (TROP2 ADC) in participants with advanced or metastatic NSCLC with confirmed EGFR mutations.

The study consists of three cohorts. It enrolls participants who have progressed after prior treatment with a third-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) and platinum-based doublet chemotherapy.

Part B enrolls participants who are currently receiving TROP2 ADC therapy or whose disease has progressed following such therapy (with no restriction on the number of prior lines).

In Part C, participants who are naïve to TROP2 ADC therapy and have received no more than three prior lines of systemic anticancer therapy will be enrolled. A safety run-in will first be conducted to confirm the safety of the combination with a TROP2 ADC. Based on the results, the Safety Review Committee (SRC) will select the recommended dose for expansion phase, which will follow Simon's two-stage design.

title: Centromere-Targeting Chimeras for Combating Cancer Drug Resistance.
authors: Zhang D, Wang Z, Feng WW et al.
abstract: Centromere protein B (CENPB), the only sequence-specific DNA-binding protein at centromeres, maintains chromosomal stability and accurate mitotic segregation. Its overexpression in aggressive cancers is associated with aneuploidy and poor prognosis, yet CENPB remains therapeutically underexplored because direct inhibitors are unavailable. Here, we develop CENPB OligoTAC, a DNA-based PROTAC comprising a CENPB-binding oligodeoxynucleotide linked to an E3 ligase ligand. CENPB OligoTAC induces ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of CENPB, disrupting centromere integrity, causing chromosome mis-segregation, and activating apoptosis. It shows potent activity in preclinical non-small cell lung cancer models resistant to first-, second-, and third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors, while exhibiting minimal cytotoxicity toward normal cells and good serum stability. In vivo, CENPB OligoTAC demonstrates favorable pharmacokinetics, good tolerability, and no significant hematological changes. By exploiting cancer cells' dependence on centromeric stability, this platform offers a novel strategy for selectively targeting aneuploid malignancies.

title: Beyond platinum sensitivity: immune-engaging therapies and multidimensional treatment stratification in relapsed small-cell lung cancer.
authors: Sun Y, Zhao X, Zhang J et al.
abstract: Although platinum sensitivity remains a convenient way to categorize relapsed small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), it no longer captures the full range of factors that may influence response to newer treatments. The interval to relapse still carries useful clinical information because it reflects the initial response, the pace of disease, and the emergence of resistance. It does not, however, identify whether a relapsed tumor can support checkpoint blockade, be efficiently recognized by a T-cell engager, or support delivery and respond to an antibody-drug conjugate (ADC). This Review considers treatment vulnerability through five interconnected features: lineage plasticity, antigen-presentation competence, T-cell function, surface-target availability, and susceptibility to the delivered payload. We integrate clinical and translational findings for DLL3-directed T-cell engagers, B7-H3-directed ADCs, and SEZ6-directed ADCs, emphasizing that resistance may arise from the target, the immune effector compartment, or the payload. We then introduce a Time-Immune-Target framework. Time represents relapse kinetics; Immune denotes the functional capacity to mount or redirect an antitumor immune response; and Target denotes the accessibility of a therapeutically relevant surface antigen. Prior therapy is superimposed on these dimensions as a record of evolutionary pressure. This proposal is intended to guide hypothesis development, not current treatment assignment. Its clinical value will need to be tested prospectively using serial tissue and blood sampling, imaging, and formal biomarker-by-treatment interaction analyses.

title: BL-DVDMS-mediated photodynamic therapy induces oxidative response associated with cellular senescence via p53/GADD45A signaling in lung cancer.
authors: Li X, Ma M, Mei Y et al.
abstract: Current chemotherapy options for lung cancer (LC) are limited by poor tumor selectivity, systemic toxicity, and acquired resistance. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) offers a promising minimally invasive modality as a potential conservative or complementary approach, yet its clinical adoption has been constrained by suboptimal photosensitizers and unclear mechanisms. This study investigated a novel PDT regimen combining a 450 nm blue laser with the photosensitizer sinoporphyrin sodium (DVDMS) to address these limitations in LC. Our findings demonstrate that BL-DVDMS treatment selectively inhibits lung cancer cell proliferation while sparing normal bronchial epithelial cells. Low-dose PDT induces a moderate oxidative stress response, leading to DNA damage and G2/M cell cycle arrest. Importantly, this treatment triggers a senescence-associated phenotype, evidenced by increased SA-β-Gal activity and elevated secretion of SASP factors (IL-6, IL-8), accompanied by altered p53/GADD45 A signaling. These effects are abrogated by ROS scavenging or p53 inhibition, indicating that the oxidative response plays a central role in the observed antitumor activity. In the subcutaneous xenograft model, this regimen significantly suppresses tumor growth with no detectable systemic toxicity. Collectively, this work identifies BL-DVDMS-mediated PDT as a mechanistically defined, senescence-associated therapeutic strategy. This study provides a potential complementary treatment option for inoperable LC patients, particularly for managing residual disease and enhancing existing therapies.

title: Single-session robotic bronchoscopy diagnoses histologically discordant synchronous lung lesions.
authors: Kanchustambham V, Saladi S, Hodkoff A
abstract: Histologically discordant synchronous pulmonary lesions in a previously treated patient may represent independent primaries, intrapulmonary metastasis, or histologic transformation. A 74-year-old woman with previously treated right upper lobe adenosquamous carcinoma developed two new, spatially separate, solid fluorodeoxyglucose-avid lesions. Both were sampled during one anaesthetic using shape-sensing robotic-assisted bronchoscopy with radial-probe endobronchial ultrasound confirmation. The peripheral right upper lobe lesion was small cell carcinoma; the left upper lobe lesion was non-small cell carcinoma, not otherwise specified, with patchy TTF-1 and p40 expression compatible with adenosquamous differentiation. Comparative clonality testing was not performed, so their relationship remained unproven. Both lesions received stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (50 Gy in five fractions); the small cell carcinoma was also treated with carboplatin and etoposide, with consolidation durvalumab planned. Bilateral sampling revealed clinically consequential histologic heterogeneity and enabled histology-directed therapy without assuming a common origin.

title: Normalized membrane ratio of TROP2 as a predictor of clinical outcomes with datopotamab deruxtecan in non-small-cell lung cancer.
authors: Garassino MC, Ahn MJ, Schick M et al.
abstract: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd)-a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody-drug conjugate-has demonstrated efficacy in patients with advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ± actionable genomic alterations. However, TROP2 expression by pathologist assessment using conventional immunohistochemistry with visual scoring does not predict response to TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugates in NSCLC. We developed TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring (QCS)-a fully supervised computational pathology approach that quantifies TROP2 expression in individual NSCLC cells and subcellular components from immunohistochemistry-stained slides. Using QCS to determine TROP2 expression at the tumor cell membrane and cytoplasm, normalized membrane ratio (NMR) was developed (ratio of membrane relative to membrane + cytoplasmic TROP2) in the biomarker-evaluable population of patients with advanced NSCLC in the TROPION-PanTumor01 study (n = 115). The TROP2 NMR cut-point was optimized and validated in patients with nonsquamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations (primary intended-use population, n = 221) in the biomarker-evaluable population (n = 352) of the TROPION-Lung01 trial. Association with clinical outcomes was assessed. Progression-free survival was longer in Dato-DXd-treated (median 7.2 versus 4.0 months; hazard ratio 0.40, 95% confidence interval 0.25-0.64) but not docetaxel-treated (median 4.1 versus 4.4 months; hazard ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.59-1.49) patients with TROP2 NMR-positive versus TROP2 NMR-negative samples (treatment by biomarker status interaction P = 0.0098), indicating that TROP2 NMR may be a predictive biomarker for Dato-DXd.

title: Postoperative complications worsen long-term survival in lung cancer surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Machida Y, Matsuda A, Okuni M et al.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Postoperative complications (POCs) are related to a poor prognosis following lung cancer surgery. This study aimed to investigate evidence of the effect of POCs on oncological outcomes, after lung cancer surgery.
METHODS: A systematic literature search of MEDLINE (PubMed), Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and ICHUSHI-Web databases up to July 2025 identified studies that compared patients with and without POCs after lung cancer surgery. Relapse-free survival and overall survival were the outcome measures. We performed a meta-analysis using random-effects models.
RESULTS: Fourteen studies involving 15,428 patients (POC group, n = 5794; no-POC group, n = 9634) were included. The overall POC rate was 37.6%. The POC group had a significantly worse relapse-free survival and overall survival than the no-POC group (hazard ratio: 1.77, 95% confidence interval: 1.40-2.25, P < 0.001 and hazard ratio: 1.67, 95% confidence interval: 1.46-1.90, P < 0.001, respectively). The relapse-free survival analysis showed statistical heterogeneity (I2 = 61%), but the sensitivity analysis showed a consistent result. A subgroup analysis showed consistently worse overall survival in the POC group.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings of this meta-analysis may help improve risk assessment for poor survival in patients after lung cancer surgery.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This systematic review and meta-analysis was registered with UMIN-CTR (ID: UMIN000058387).

title: Development of a multidisciplinary service-delivery framework for venous thromboembolism prevention in hospitalized medical patients with lung cancer: a mixed-methods modified Delphi study.
authors: Meng Y, Zhong S, Ding Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a common and potentially preventable complication in patients with lung cancer. Although clinical guidelines recommend risk assessment and appropriate prophylaxis, hospitals often lack operational frameworks for translating these recommendations into multidisciplinary workflows, quality monitoring, and continuous improvement. This study aimed to develop a hospital-based multidisciplinary service-delivery framework for VTE prevention and management among hospitalized medical patients with lung cancer.
METHODS: A mixed-methods modified Delphi study was conducted. Candidate framework items were generated from a structured literature review and semi-structured interviews with physicians, nurses, clinical pharmacists, and hospital managers, and were organized using Donabedian's Structure-Process-Outcome model. A two-round Delphi survey was then conducted with 15 experts from respiratory medicine, oncology, clinical pharmacy, nursing management, and hospital quality management. Experts rated the importance and feasibility of each candidate item, and the framework was refined using predefined consensus criteria and qualitative feedback.
RESULTS: The response rate was 100% in both Delphi rounds. Expert authority coefficients were 0.943 and 0.953 in rounds 1 and 2, respectively. Kendall's W ranged from 0.249 to 0.292, indicating low-to-moderate concordance despite statistically significant tests. The final framework included 3 first-level domains, 11 second-level components, and 34 third-level indicators covering structural capacity, care processes, and outcome monitoring. Importance ratings were generally higher than feasibility ratings, particularly for indicators requiring information system support, multidisciplinary coordination, and post-discharge continuity of care.
CONCLUSION: This study developed a preliminary, consensus-based multidisciplinary service-delivery framework for hospital-based VTE prevention in patients with lung cancer. The framework may support the operationalization of guideline recommendations, standardization of care processes, and prioritization of quality improvement efforts. Prospective implementation studies are needed to evaluate its feasibility, transferability, and impact on care quality and patient outcomes.

title: Effectiveness and Safety of Early Bed Resistance Exercise after Lung Cancer Surgery.
authors: Wang Y, Luo J, Yan Y et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the application effectiveness and safety of early bedside resistance exercise in postoperative rehabilitation for patients with lung cancer. Study Design: A non-randomised controlled trial. Place and Duration of the Study: Department of Thoracic Surgery, Guangxi Medical University Cancer Hospital, Nanning, China, from January to October 2025.
METHODOLOGY: One hundred and fifty-seven lung cancer patients who underwent thoracoscopic lobectomy at a tertiary cancer hospital's thoracic surgery department were enrolled. The control group (n = 80) received routine postoperative exercise rehabilitation care; the experimental group (n = 77) additionally received phased early bed resistance training. Mann-Whitney U test was used for non-normally distributed variables, the t-test for normally distributed variables, and the chi-square test for intergroup exercise safety outcomes. To adjust for potential confounding arising from the non-randomised design, multivariable regression, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), and doubly robust estimation were performed; effect sizes and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for between-group comparisons.
RESULTS: The experimental group showed a smaller postoperative decrease in handgrip strength on the non-operated side and a higher 48-hour postoperative chest tube drainage volume than the control group (p <0.05). After adjustment for confounders, the intervention group showed a smaller decline in handgrip strength on the non-operated side (adjusted median difference -1.29 kg, 95% CI: -2.48 to -0.11; p = 0.032), consistent with IPTW (p = 0.020) and doubly robust (p = 0.013) sensitivity analyses. The between-group difference in 48-hour postoperative chest tube drainage volume was no longer statistically significant after adjustment (p = 0.077). No significant between-group differences were found in total chest tube drainage volume, coagulation function, vital-sign fluctuations, or other safety indicators (all p >0.05), and no serious adverse events occurred in either group.
CONCLUSION: Early bed resistance exercise may attenuate postoperative decline in muscle strength and appears to be safe, providing a complementary exercise option for patients unable to ambulate early. Its effect on thoracic drainage volume requires further investigation. These findings support its potential use in postoperative rehabilitation. Key Words: Lung cancer, Thoracoscopic surgery, Early bed resistance exercise, Postoperative rehabilitation.

title: Zone-specific lymph node metastasis prediction model in clinical stage I-II non-small cell lung cancer: a supplementary analysis of JCOG1413.
authors: Isaka M, Hishida T, Saji H et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal extent of lymph node dissection in early-stage non-small cell lung cancer remains unclear. We aimed to develop zone-specific lymph node metastasis prediction models for clinical stage I-II non-small cell lung cancer using data from the Japan Clinical Oncology Group (JCOG) 1413, a randomized phase III trial comparing lobe-specific and systematic lymph node dissection.
METHODS: The analysis included 1699 eligible cases out of 1711 patients from 44 institutions in JCOG1413. Leave-one-out cross-validation was used to evaluate the prediction algorithm, and multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of metastasis for constructing nomograms. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves with concordance statistics and calibration curves with calibration slope.
RESULTS: We developed models for four zones: upper (including the aortopulmonary zone) (n = 1416), subcarinal (n = 1170), hilar (n = 1662), and peripheral (n = 1662). Common independent predictors included histology, maximum standardized uptake on positron emission tomography, and, particularly for mediastinal zones, primary tumor lobe location. The subcarinal zone showed the best performance, with a concordance statistic of 0.7902 and a calibration slope of 1.0762. Across all zones, calibration slopes remained close to 1.0, and negative predictive values ranged from 96.6% to 99.4%.
CONCLUSIONS: Zone-specific prediction models demonstrated moderate discrimination and well-calibrated estimates of lymph-node metastasis risk, with the highest performance observed in the subcarinal zone. These models could support risk stratification and facilitate individualized intraoperative nodal assessment to inform clinical decision-making.

title: Association between perioperative six-minute walk distance and postoperative recurrence and survival in patients with lung cancer.
authors: Fujiwara K, Saito T, Ueda Y et al.
abstract:
PURPOSE: The prognostic value of perioperative exercise capacity in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains unclear. We examined associations between preoperative and early postoperative six-minute walk distance (6MWD) and recurrence and survival.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 133 patients with NSCLC who underwent pulmonary resection and completed preoperative and/or predischarge six-minute walk tests. Outcomes were relapse-free survival (RFS), overall survival (OS), and time to recurrence (TTR). Cox models evaluated continuous 6MWD, adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, pathological stage, and adjuvant chemotherapy. Secondary 3-year Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed using cohort medians (485 m preoperatively and 445 m postoperatively).
RESULTS: The preoperative and postoperative cohorts included 75 and 123 patients, respectively; 65 belonged to both. Longer preoperative 6MWD was associated with RFS (hazard ratio [HR] per 50-m increase, 0.734; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.541-0.994; p = 0.046) and OS (HR, 0.597; 95% CI, 0.391-0.912; p = 0.017), but not TTR. Longer early postoperative 6MWD was associated with RFS (HR, 0.592; 95% CI, 0.469-0.748; p < 0.001), OS (HR, 0.692; 95% CI, 0.514-0.933; p = 0.016), and TTR (HR, 0.657; 95% CI, 0.509-0.848; p = 0.001). In parsimonious sensitivity analyses, the preoperative RFS and OS associations and postoperative OS association were attenuated, whereas postoperative RFS and TTR remained significant. Postoperative recurrence findings persisted in competing-risk and landmark analyses.
CONCLUSIONS: Perioperative 6MWD showed exploratory associations with RFS and TTR. Evidence for an association with OS remained inconclusive; validation in larger prospective studies is needed.

title: Inhalable ivermectin-loaded lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles as a promising anticancer platform for non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Kassaee SN, Richard DJ, Ayoko GA et al.
abstract: Pulmonary drug delivery offers a compelling strategy for lung diseases including lung cancer, which remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortalities worldwide, by enabling direct tumour site targeting, avoidance of first-pass metabolism, and high local drug concentrations with reduced systemic toxicity. In this study, inhalable ivermectin-loaded lipid-polymer hybrid nanoparticles (IVM-LPHNPs) were investigated in A549 and H460 non-small cell lung cancer cell lines (NSCLC). Cellular uptake was examined by confocal microscopy and flow cytometry, while in vitro therapeutic efficacy was evaluated through cell viability, wound healing, and colony formation assays to determine their anticancer, anti-proliferative, anti-migratory, and anti-clonogenic activities. Cellular uptake analysis confirmed improved intracellular accumulation of coumarin-6 loaded -LPHNPs relative to free coumarin-6. Moreover, IVM-LPHNPs demonstrated approximately 20% reduction in IC50 compared to free ivermectin, while blank LPHNPs did not reduce viability. Developed formulations showed no considerable toxicity to human bronchial epithelial cells, confirming the safety of LPHNPs for healthy lung cells. Furthermore, more than 50% reduction in clonogenic survival and significantly greater inhibition of cell proliferation and migration was observed in IVM-loaded LPHNPs compared to free IVM. Collectively, these findings position IVM-LPHNPs as a promising inhalable platform for the localized treatment of NSCLC, warranting further investigation in preclinical models.

title: Corticosteroid-refractory checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis in lung cancer: biological heterogeneity and mechanism-informed management.
authors: Zhang R, Zhang X, He X et al.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of lung cancer, but checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) remains a potentially life-threatening immune-related adverse event. A subset of patients fails to improve despite adequate glucocorticoid therapy and develops corticosteroid-refractory CIP, which is associated with respiratory failure, substantial mortality, and considerable therapeutic uncertainty. This review critically examines the clinical definition, phenotypic characteristics, immunological mechanisms, and therapeutic evidence for corticosteroid-refractory CIP. Emerging data suggest that refractoriness should not be regarded as a uniform failure of glucocorticoid treatment, but rather as a biologically heterogeneous and dynamically evolving syndrome involving persistent tissue-resident T-cell activation, inflammatory T-cell-myeloid crosstalk, cytokine-network redundancy, innate immune dysregulation, and, in some patients, transition toward maladaptive tissue repair and structural lung remodeling. Current second-line treatments, including mycophenolate mofetil, infliximab, intravenous immunoglobulin, tocilizumab, cyclophosphamide, and calcineurin inhibitors, are supported predominantly by retrospective studies and case-report and case-series evidence, with no established optimal treatment sequence. We therefore propose a hypothesis-generating phenotype-to-therapy framework that distinguishes lymphocyte-dominant, cytokine-dominant, fulminant acute lung injury/diffuse alveolar damage, innate/myeloid-dominant, and organizing/fibrotic-remodeling phenotypes while recognizing their potential overlap and temporal evolution. Translating this framework into clinical practice will require harmonized definitions, longitudinal multimodal phenotyping, treatment-predictive biomarkers, and prospective comparative studies. Ultimately, management should move beyond empirical escalation of immunosuppression toward identifying the dominant biological process at a given disease stage and matching treatment intensity and mechanism accordingly.

title: Reduced classical probiotic-associated butyrate biosynthetic potential predicts early primary resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a shotgun metagenomic study.
authors: Mei Y, Shi L, He S et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early primary resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy is common in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Existing microbiome biomarkers largely rely on individual species and lack stability across populations.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to construct the classical probiotic-butyrate axis score (PBAS), perform external validation, and evaluate its value for risk stratification of 90-day early primary resistance and PFS.
METHODS: This study adopted a dual-cohort, patient-level secondary analysis design and reanalyzed pretreatment fecal shotgun metagenomic data from two public cohorts, including 70 and 40 patients in the discovery and external validation cohorts, respectively. An equally weighted PBAS was constructed based on predefined classical probiotic-associated taxa and the butyryl-CoA:acetate CoA-transferase (but) and the butyrate kinase (buk) genes. ANCOM-BC2 was used for differential analysis, Firth logistic regression for association analysis of early primary resistance, 2,000 patient-level bootstrap resampling for internal validation, and Cox proportional hazards models for PFS analysis.
RESULTS: Early primary resistance occurred in 41/70 and 23/40 patients in the two cohorts, respectively. Classical probiotic-associated taxa, the butyrate functional subscore, and PBAS were lower in the resistant group than in the nonresistant group, whereas buk and Akkermansia muciniphila showed no significant differences. After adjustment for age, sex, and BMI, acetyl-CoA pathway potential was also reduced. For each 1-SD increase in PBAS, the OR for early primary resistance was 0.39 and 0.37 after adjustment for clinical variables. The bootstrap-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.733, and the external validation AUC was 0.726 (95% CI: 0.559-0.894). Increased PBAS was associated with a lower risk of progression or death, with HRs of 0.54 and 0.61 in the two cohorts, respectively (both p < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Combined reductions in pretreatment classical probiotic-associated ecology and butyrate biosynthetic potential indicate a high risk of early primary resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in advanced NSCLC and support PBAS as an exploratory outcome risk marker for cross-cohort risk stratification among patients receiving anti-PD-1 therapy, without establishing treatment-specific predictive value.

title: Upregulation of SLC35A2 facilitates malignant progression and autophagy in lung adenocarcinoma.
authors: Xu Y, Sun X, Chen Z et al.
abstract: ObjectiveSolute carrier family 35 member A2 (SLC35A2), a glycosylation-associated transporter, has been implicated in the progression of several malignancies, but its role in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the clinical significance and biological function of SLC35A2 in LUAD.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 80 patients with histologically confirmed LUAD. SLC35A2 expression and its association with clinicopathological characteristics and survival were evaluated. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments assessed LUAD cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and a nude mouse xenograft model evaluated tumor growth in vivo. Autophagy-related proteins, tandem fluorescent LC3 puncta, and the effects of chloroquine treatment were examined. A prognostic model incorporating independent prognostic factors was internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples.ResultsSLC35A2 was upregulated in LUAD tissues and associated with adverse clinicopathological features and poor overall survival. Multivariate Cox analysis identified SLC35A2 as an independent prognostic factor. The model had an apparent C-index of 0.714 and an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.684. SLC35A2 overexpression enhanced LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and xenograft growth, whereas its depletion produced the opposite effects. Overexpression was associated with a higher LC3-II/LC3-I ratio, increased Beclin1, reduced p62, and more yellow LC3 puncta per cell; the difference in red-only puncta was not statistically significant. Chloroquine reduced CCK-8 signals in SLC35A2-overexpressing cells.ConclusionsSLC35A2 promotes malignant phenotypes in LUAD and is associated with autophagy-related changes. These findings support its potential as a prognostic biomarker and candidate therapeutic target, while the contribution of autophagy to its tumor-promoting effects requires further mechanistic validation.

title: Advances on the Intrapleural Management of Malignant Pleural Disease.
authors: Nguyen DTH, Puppo G, Pinelli V et al.
abstract: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) and malignant pleural disease (MPD) are common complications of cancer. Although they may significantly affect the quality of life, treatment options remain limited. Official guidelines recommend effusion drainage and pleurodesis, and, while they may achieve symptomatic relief, their impact on disease progression is limited. Intrapleural therapy has been studied for several decades due to its theoretical (and proven) superior local drug retention, maximising drug exposure. Recent works on intrapleural administration include exploring novel therapeutic agents and administration methods, such as hyperthermic intrathoracic chemotherapy (HITHOC) and pressurised intrathoracic chemotherapy (PITAC). These therapies directly modulate the tumour environments. Promising intrapleural candidates include targeted and immunotherapies such as CAR (chimeric antigen receptor)-T cells, PD-1 (programmed death protein 1) inhibitors, and IL-6 (interleukin-6) inhibitors. However, the level of evidence remains mixed, requiring further studies and quantitative synthesis.

title: Clinical development landscape of CAR/TCR-engineered cellular therapies in musculoskeletal sarcomas: a TrialTrove-based registry analysis.
authors: Jia X, Chen Q, Wang Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: CAR/TCR-engineered cellular therapies are increasingly investigated in musculoskeletal sarcomas, but the clinical development portfolio spans heterogeneous histologies, platforms, antigens, and basket protocols. We mapped the TrialTrove-derived landscape while explicitly separating engineered-receptor products from other cell-based immunotherapies.
METHODS: TrialTrove clinical trial data were retrieved on 10 June 2026 and constituted the sole data source. Candidate records were identified using prespecified musculoskeletal-sarcoma disease terms and CAR/TCR-engineered-cell product terms. Two investigators independently assessed eligibility and assigned standardized classifications, with disagreements adjudicated by a third investigator. Potential duplicate representations were evaluated using TrialTrove, NCT, and normalized secondary identifiers plus study-level characteristics. We summarized temporal, geographic, phase, status, sponsor, protocol-planned enrollment, platform, target, disease-scope, co-intervention, concentration, and field-availability characteristics. Broader solid-tumor records with explicit sarcoma eligibility were reported separately, the export did not permit consistent determination of actual sarcoma enrollment or a dedicated sarcoma cohort.
RESULTS: Of 140 identified records, 121 were eligible: 38 (31.4%) were sarcoma-specific and 83 (68.6%) were broader solid-tumour records with explicit sarcoma eligibility. Among 110 records with a start year, 63 (57.3%) began during 2021-2026. Phase I or I/II accounted for 108/121 records (89.3%), and median protocol-planned enrollment was 24 participants (IQR 15-49, n=103). The United States and China contributed 55.2% of 163 trial-country links. TCR-T and CAR-T accounted for 60 (49.6%) and 52 (43.0%) records, respectively. NY-ESO-1 contributed 45/125 trial-target links (36.0%), after excluding 12 Unspecified reporting links, the three most frequent specified antigens contributed 66/113 specified-antigen links (58.4%).
CONCLUSIONS: Engineered cellular-therapy development in musculoskeletal sarcomas has accelerated but remains predominantly early phase, geographically and antigenically concentrated, and represented largely by broader solid-tumour protocols that list sarcoma eligibility. Prespecified sarcoma strata, dedicated and independently analyzable cohorts, biomarker enrichment, harmonized outcomes, and transparent adjunct-strategy reporting should strengthen future evidence generation. This TrialTrove-based record analysis does not establish actual sarcoma enrollment in basket protocols, comparative efficacy, clinical superiority of a platform or antigen, or exhaustive global coverage.

title: A Research-Integrated Curriculum on CAR-T Cell Therapy.
authors: Khan YH, Rice L, Srougi MC
abstract: Cell-based cancer immunotherapies such as chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy are an established and evolving class of cancer treatment, yet few cancer education curricula give students hands-on experience with the laboratory methods that underlie them. To address this gap, we developed and implemented a novel, small-enrollment curriculum designed to teach upper-level undergraduate and graduate students about immunotherapies and CAR-T cell technology by paralleling a typical bench-scale development process. Students isolated T cells from porcine peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) via immunomagnetic selection, followed by flow cytometry to assess purity, viability, and yield. Students then used pre-engineered B7H3 CAR-T cells to perform co-culture assays with U87 glioblastoma cells to evaluate tumor cell killing efficacy. Cytotoxicity was qualitatively evaluated using immunofluorescence microscopy, while IFN-γ release was quantified using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Student performance was evaluated through electronic laboratory notebooks, discussion questions, a capstone project, and student-generated data. Our results demonstrate students' high academic performance across assignments and the successful execution of complex laboratory workflows. Collectively, these findings establish the feasibility and implementation of a research-integrated curriculum providing foundational exposure to immuno-oncology research tools and CAR-T cell production techniques.

title: Immune niche remodeling: sustaining CAR-T persistence in solid tumors.
authors: Kim HC, Kim D, Bae J et al.

title: Temporal control of CAR expression by a tumor-targeting albumin adapter and logic gating enhances CAR-T cell therapy for solid tumors.
authors: Chen J, Zhao L, Shen C et al.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cell therapy has shown limited efficacy against solid tumors, with T cell exhaustion representing a major barrier. Both tonic and persistent antigen-dependent CAR signaling markedly drive T cell exhaustion. We therefore hypothesize that minimizing CAR expression (CE) before tumor entry and inducing pulses of CE within tumors would mitigate exhaustion caused by both signaling modes. Here, we present modular artificial- and natural-antigen-gated (MANAGE) CAR-T cells that employ a fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-sensing synNotch receptor to gate CE. Modulating the dosing schedule of FITC-modified tumor-targeting priming adapters enables tumor-restricted and temporally programmable CE in vivo. Compared with constitutive CAR-T and endogenous-antigen-gated synNotch CAR-T cells, temporally tuned MANAGE CAR-T cells exhibit substantially reduced exhaustion and greater preservation of stem-like phenotypes. MANAGE CAR-T cells primed with an albumin-based adapter achieve complete responses without overt toxicity in immunologically "cold" breast cancer and glioblastoma models. This modular strategy is adaptable to various engineered immune cell modalities.

title: Transactivation of EGFR by LCK underlies an activity-defined dependency that predicts response to EGFR inhibition in cholangiocarcinoma
summary: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is an aggressive biliary tract malignancy with limited molecularly guided treatment options. The Src-family kinase LCK is a therapeutic vulnerability in CCA, yet its canonical T-cell substrates are minimally expressed in CCA cells, leaving its downstream effectors undefined. Unbiased proximity labeling in HuCCT1 cells identified EGFR within the LCK signaling neighborhood. LCK depletion or inhibition reduced EGFR phosphorylation, whereas recombinant LCK increased EGFR phosphorylation in a cell-free assay, supporting a noncanonical role for LCK upstream of EGFR. Given the failure of EGFR-directed therapies in unselected CCA populations, we hypothesized that EGFR activity, rather than abundance or mutation status, identifies EGFR-dependent tumors. Among 28 patient-derived xenografts ranked by pretreatment substrate-inferred EGFR activity, the activity score correctly classified afatinib response in all six models tested. An analogous EGFR activity score stratified primary tumors in two human CCA cohorts. Together, these findings identify a therapeutically actionable LCK-EGFR signaling axis and nominate EGFR activity as a functional biomarker to guide tumor selection for EGFR-directed therapy in CCA, warranting prospective clinical validation.

title: Density dependence and evolvability limit adaptive therapy in non-small cell lung cancer mouse model.
authors: Pressley M, Cunningham JJ, Simoes L et al.
abstract:
UNLABELLED: Using NSG mice grafted with H3122 non-small cell lung cancer cells, we compared outcomes from (1) continuous therapy with alectinib, (2) adaptive therapy where alectinib was cycled on and off based on a mouse's tumor burden, and (3) no treatment. Adaptive therapy has proven successful in mouse models and clinical trials. The success of adaptive therapy improves when either there is density-dependent feedbacks favoring competition by sensitive over resistant cancer cells when therapy is off, or when the rate at which the population of cancer cells becomes more sensitive to therapy during periods of no treatment is faster than the rate at which resistance increases when on therapy. We found tumor growth rates were lowest under continuous therapy and highest under no therapy with adaptive therapy in between. We fitted the data to three separate game-theory models of resistance evolution where we let resistance be a quantitative trait consistent with resistance mechanisms to alectinib. All models successfully identified why adaptive therapy proved less successful than continuous: there was no evidence for favorable density-dependent feedbacks; and there was no significant difference in the rate of evolution towards or away from resistance when therapy was on or off.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-63987-x.

title: Interpreting survival and recurrence after resection of anaplastic lymphoma kinase-rearranged non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Rahman M, Asif N

title: A Cuproptosis Nanoparticle Reverses Lung Adenocarcinoma Drug Resistance.
authors: Wu L, Li K, Wang H et al.
abstract: Residual tumors that received targeted therapy often evolve into drug resistance, with an increasing risk of recurrence and metastasis. By analyzing patient data, it is found that KRAS-mutated lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) exhibits a worse survival rate than wild-type LUAD. Although the clinical drug AMG-510 has been approved to treat KRAS(G12C)-mutated LUAD, its effectiveness is still limited by drug resistance. Cuproptosis, a newly identified mode of cellular death, shows promise in cancer treatment and in reversing drug resistance. By comparing cell lines with different sensitivities to AMG-510, we discovered that ATP7B, a key regulator of cuproptosis, was up-regulated in AMG-510-resistant cell lines to decrease their sensitivity to cuproptosis. Therefore, a targeted sensitization strategy focused on cuproptosis was proposed using a single nanoparticle based on bovine serum albumin encapsulating copper ions (termed CuNPs). Both in vitro and in vivo results demonstrated that these nanoparticles released copper ions in an acidic environment, and the following CuNP-triggered cuproptosis could effectively down-regulated ATP7B, which successfully overcame AMG-510 resistance with a synergistic antitumor effect. Collectively, targeting cuproptosis in KRAS-mutated lung adenocarcinoma emerges as a compelling strategy to address drug resistance.

title: Spark-like T cell represents a novel functional state of CD8+T cells associated with anti-PD-1 immunotherapy response and clinical prognosis in non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Li Z, Li R, Sun F et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spark-like T cells constitute a novel functional state of CD8+T cells and have emerged as key drivers of immunotherapy response in preclinical models, yet their clinical relevance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains undefined.
METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE207422), spatial transcriptomics (GSE271689), bulk RNA expression cohorts (TCGA-NSCLC, GSE37745, GSE41271, and GSE72094), and multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC) of a 100-patient cohort treated with anti-PD-1 were integrated to characterize Spark-like T cells and assess their clinical relevance. A 14-gene prognostic signature was constructed via LASSO-Cox regression.
RESULTS: Spark-like T cells were significantly enriched in anti-PD-1 responders in the single-cell RNA sequencing cohort. mIHC validation in the 100-patient cohort confirmed that high Spark-like T cell intensity in tumors was independently associated with prolonged overall survival (log-rank test, p < 0.001) and partial response to anti-PD-1 therapy (p = 0.0075). Spatial transcriptomics indicated strong co-localization of Spark-like T cells with M1 macrophages (Spearman r = 0.524, p = 3.4 × 10-42), suggesting their spatial co-enrichment with pro-inflammatory myeloid cells. In silico knockout identified TNF, ENTPD1 (CD39), and IL2 as cooperative regulators of Spark-like T cell effector function. The 14-gene Spark-like T cell-related signature (VDAC1, ITGB1, GALNT2, SEMA7A, UBB, SLC7A5, FURIN, SNX9, PSMB2, CXCL13, TOX, PPM1M, CCND2, and CLNK) robustly predicted overall survival across all four independent cohorts and remained an independent prognostic factor after adjustment for age, sex, and tumor stage. High-risk patients exhibited an immune-excluded, oncogene-driven tumor microenvironment with reduced infiltration of CD8+T cells.
CONCLUSIONS: Spark-like T cells are clinically relevant determinants of anti-PD-1 response in NSCLC. mIHC quantification and the 14-gene signature provide promising translational tools for patient stratification and risk assessment.

title: CIP2A drives lung adenocarcinoma by activating mitochondrial respiratory complexes IV and V.
authors: Yang FY, Wang D, Ye L et al.
abstract: To determine the cancer-initiating activity of oncoprotein CIP2A, which is overexpressed in a majority of cancers and promotes cell growth by stabilizing MYC, we established an alveolar type 2 cell-specific CIP2A transgenic mouse line. Among 114 transgenic mice aged 12 months or older, 23 (20.2%) developed lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD)-like disease, significantly higher than in the control mice (3/63, 4.8%). Multi-omic studies revealed enrichment of the oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) pathway in tumor tissues from transgenic mice. CIP2A upregulated phosphorylation of FOXO3A (p-FOXO3A S253) by inhibiting phosphatase PP2A-B56α and promoted FOXO3A mitochondrial translocation. CIP2A-FOXO3A reshaped mitochondrial morphology, activated mitochondrial DNA transcription, and enhanced complexes IV/V activities. OXPHOS inhibitor repressed CIP2A-induced cell proliferation and tumor growth. Moreover, tobacco carcinogens upregulated CIP2A and p-FOXO3A S253 and significantly increased cancer incidence in CIP2A-transgenic mice. These data indicate that CIP2A plays a critical role in mitochondrial regulation and represents a promising therapeutic target for LUADs lacking actionable driver mutations.

title: Transcriptional landscape of nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma and T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma: tumor microenvironment and checkpoint genes.
authors: Kalashnikov I, Russell V, Kositsky R et al.
abstract: Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL) is a rare B-cell malignancy with an indolent course, yet some cases relapse or transform to Tcell/ histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma (THRLBCL). Biological factors underlying poor outcomes in NLPHL are largely unknown, and the relationship between THRLBCL and untransformed NLPHL has not been systematically defined. We analyzed 178 NLPHL and 22 THRLBCL cases using whole-transcriptome RNA sequencing and clinical data. NLPHL patients were younger, had limited-stage disease, and better outcomes than THRLBCL patients. Variant immuno-architectural patterns (IAP) in NLPHL showed THRLBCL-like transcriptional profiles, especially with splenic involvement and high Lymphocyte-Predominant International Prognostic Score (LP-IPS). In-silico deconvolution of the tumor microenvironment (TME) revealed B-cell enrichment in classic NLPHL, intermediate profiles in variant NLPHL, and increased activated CD4+ and CD8+ T-cells and macrophages in THRLBCL. Higher follicular helper T-cell content was associated with shorter event-free survival in an exploratory analysis. NLPHL cases showed strong B-cell and T-helper signatures, whereas THRLBCL cases were enriched for macrophage and cytotoxic T-cell pathways and expressed higher immune checkpoint genes, suggesting an immunosuppressive TME. Signatures defined a spectrum from classic to variant NLPHL and THRLBCL. External validation in independent cohorts reproduced this gradient, supporting a continuous microenvironmental spectrum spanning NLPHL and THRLBCL.

title: NCAM1 potentiates small cell lung cancer stemness and resistance to NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity.
authors: Qi J, Sun H, Yang Y et al.
abstract: Intrinsic resistance of small cell lung cancer (SCLC) to immunotherapy underscores our limited understanding of how tumors can evade immune responses. Here we demonstrated that neural cell adhesion molecule 1 (NCAM1, also called CD56) facilitates disease progression, tumor stemness, and resistance to NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity in SCLC. Mechanistically, cis-binding of NCAM1 with its ligand L1CAM on the surface of identical tumor cell occupied considerable antigenic epitopes of L1CAM, and thereby prevented L1CAM from trans-binding with CD56+ NK cells to form immune-synapse structures, which may render the tumor cells more resistant to NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity in SCLC. Additionally, CHMP4B, a member of the ESCRT complex involved in plasma membrane repair, were essential for SCLC stemness and NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity, and NCAM1 can protect SCLC cells from immune attack and stem cell renewal by interacting with CHMP4B. SCLC specimens with concurrent high expression of NCAM1 and CHMP4B exhibited lower cytotoxic immune cell infiltration, were located farther from cytotoxic immune cells, and were associated with inferior clinical outcomes. These findings reveal potential mechanisms of NCAM1 in sustaining SCLC stemness and resisting cytolytic attack, and provide a potential target of CHMP4B against self-renewal and immunoresistance.

title: Paraneoplastic Neurological Syndrome Associated with Probable Small Cell Lung Cancer Initially Misdiagnosed as Disuse Syndrome and Delirium: A Case Report.
authors: Kiyuna T, Kami W, Furugen M et al.
abstract: Paraneoplastic neurological syndrome (PNS) is an immune-mediated disorder in which neurological symptoms often precede tumor detection. We report the case of a 78-year-old woman with a history of heavy smoking and prior malignancy who presented with progressive cognitive impairment, athetosis, and conjugate eye deviation. She had been managed for disuse syndrome and delirium for six months before chest computed tomography (CT) revealed a right hilar mass. Paraneoplastic antibody testing revealed positivity for CV2/CRMP5, Ri, titin, and Zic4 antibodies, and she was clinically diagnosed with PNS. Recognizing the atypical features of delirium may prompt an earlier evaluation of PNS.

title: Risk-adapted multimodality care for elderly limited-stage small-cell lung cancer.
authors: Hsu CX, Kao YT, Shueng PW et al.

title: Immune-Related Adverse Events: Findings From a Population-Based Study.
authors: Heinzerling L, Seemann IT, Ingram A et al.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are effective for several tumor entities but cause immune-related adverse events (irAEs). These side effects may affect any organ and often lead to ICI discontinuation, hospitalization, long-term complications, or sequelae. To assess the burden of irAEs, this longitudinal observational study analyzed their incidence and the frequency of related hospitalizations using anonymized health claims data from a payer database covering 5.8 million insured individuals in Germany. Patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), renal cancer, urothelial cancer, or skin cancer who started ICI therapy between 2017 and 2020 were selected using ICD-10 GM (International Statistical Classification of Diseases, German Modification) codes. The incidence of irAEs and related hospitalizations within 6 months was assessed using predefined ICD-10 codes in both inpatient and outpatient settings. A total of 6350 patients (mean age: 66.8 y) with NSCLC (n=4797), skin cancer (n=1266), HCC (n=1249), renal (n=1183), or urothelial cancer (n=656) initiated ICI therapy between 2017 and 2020. The incidence of any new-onset irAE was 31.4% (95% CI: 30.3%-32.6%). New-onset respiratory irAEs were the most common [11.7% (95% CI: 11.0%-12.5%)], followed by gastrointestinal irAEs (7.8%; 95% CI: 7.1%-8.5%). Skin cancer patients most frequently developed gastrointestinal irAEs, while other tumor types showed more respiratory irAEs. Using an inclusive definition that also captures exacerbations of pre-existing conditions, nearly half of patients experienced at least one hospitalization with an irAE recorded as the main discharge diagnosis within 6 months after ICI initiation. These findings underscore the importance of monitoring and management to reduce patient and healthcare impact.

title: Immune-related hepatitis and HLA-DQB1*06:01 as potential predictor biomarkers in East Asian patients with lung cancer treated with ICIs: a large-scale real-world study.
authors: Yan H, Zhou G, Wu Y et al.

title: Impact of lung cancer screening on the workload of radiology professionals.
authors: Tong EWY, Nischwitz E, Kerpel-Fronius A et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Lung cancer screening (LCS) with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) significantly reduces mortality among high-risk individuals, yet implementation remains limited at national and European levels. The Strengthening the Screening of Lung Cancer (SOLACE) Project aims to facilitate the implementation of equitable LCS. While considering the overall impact of LCS, we identified a lack of systematic evaluation on the impact on the workload of radiology professionals, including radiologists and radiographers. This multicentric, European-wide study prospectively examines the effects of LCS on radiology healthcare workers.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A survey-based cross-sectional study was conducted among European radiology professionals engaged in LCS to evaluate their experiences across seven domains: impacts on workload, workflow specifics, reporting practices, artificial intelligence (AI) use, participation in training programmes, potential professional development, and overall support for LCS.
RESULTS: We evaluated 56 responses (mean age 46 ± 10.8 years; 27 men) from 14 countries. About half of respondents (53.6%; n = 30) reported increased working hours, but only 21.6% (n = 11) felt overworked due to LCS. No significant factors were directly associated with feeling overworked. Most respondents (86.7%; n = 39) perceived increased expertise in assessing LCS LDCTs throughout screening, and 91.1% (n = 51) expressed support for the implementation of LCS.
CONCLUSION: Although LCS increased workload for many radiology professionals, few reported feeling overworked. Despite the added demands, there may be added benefits for radiology professionals. Taken together, these findings emphasise the importance of continuously evaluating and monitoring how LCS affects the workload of radiology healthcare professionals.
KEY POINTS: Question As wider implementation of lung cancer screening occurs in Europe, it is critical to consider its impact on radiology professionals' workload and associated workforce demands. Findings Although lung cancer screening increased workload for many radiology professionals, few felt overworked, and the majority perceived increased diagnostic confidence and support for screening implementation.
CRITICAL RELEVANCE STATEMENT: Lung cancer screening via LDCT plays a critical role in detecting cancer earlier and improving survival. With growing support for the broader implementation of LCS, it is essential to consider its potential impact on the workload of radiology professionals.

title: Indoor radon monitoring through citizen science in Catalan schools: environmental assessment and educational outcomes.
authors: Javed M, Martínez I, Jimenez A et al.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Indoor radon represents a significant environmental health hazard because high indoor radon concentration exposure increases lung cancer risk. Schools are critical settings due to prolonged occupancy by children. The RASCLET citizen-science project (Catalonia, Spain) integrated school-based radon monitoring with educational activities to evaluate exposure conditions and examine whether these activities increased radon knowledge and risk awareness. Meteorological variables and modeled radon flux were also explored in relation to indoor radon variability.
METHODS: Integrated radon measurements were conducted in 13 schools across Catalonia (Spain) during the winter of 2024-2025. Detectors were placed in classrooms on different floors. Schools represented different radon risk areas defined by official Spanish radon potential maps. At each school, approximately 40 students participated in educational activities about radon under their teacher's supervision. Students and their teacher then selected the classrooms where detectors would be installed. Pre and post-intervention questionnaires assessed changes in students' knowledge and perceptions of radon risks.
RESULTS: Indoor radon concentrations varied across schools and floor levels, with a median concentration of 49 Bq m-3 (interquartile range: 24-77 Bq m-3). All measurements obtained during the winter monitoring period remained below the 300 Bq m-3 reference level. PRE and POST-intervention questionnaires were completed by 538 and 339 students, respectively. The mean age was 11.07 ± 1.18 years (PRE) and 10.99 ± 1.04 years (POST), with female-to-male distributions of 49.4%/46.8 and 48.7%/48.7%, respectively. Correct identification of radon as a radioactive gas increased from 34.2 to 72.9% and recognition of its long-term health effects increased from 42.0 to 85.5% (both p < 0.001). Additionally, indoor radon data, combined with meteorological and radon flux data, were used in an exploratory modelling analysis. The analysis identified wind speed as the only statistically significant environmental variable associated with observed indoor radon concentrations (p = 0.025).
CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that integrating school-based radon monitoring with citizen-science and educational activities can support exposure assessment, strengthen environmental health literacy, and improve radon risk communication in educational settings. This pilot study also provides a rationale for designing and conducting a larger-scale study across Spain to further evaluate this integrated approach.

title: Lattice radiotherapy boost integrated with thoracic VMAT in bulky stage IIIB non-small cell lung cancer: a case report.
authors: Wang S, Li XC, Ran JT et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bulky unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) presents a clinical challenge during definitive radiotherapy, as homogeneous dose escalation is often constrained by organ-at-risk (OAR) tolerance. Spatially fractionated radiotherapy (SFRT), including lattice radiotherapy (LRT), creates an intratumoral peak-valley dose distribution and may provide a means to intensify local dose delivery. However, the optimal dose, fractionation, vertex geometry, treatment sequence, and contribution of LRT to clinical response remain uncertain.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a 41-year-old never-smoking Han Chinese man with bulky unresectable stage IIIB (cT4N2M0, AJCC 8th edition) disease, with a primary tumor measuring 71×53 mm at baseline. After two cycles of induction platinum-based chemotherapy, the disease was classified as stable disease. The patient subsequently received thoracic VMAT to 60 Gy in 15 fractions, during this course, a LRT plan was interleaved within the VMAT plan and delivered using an interleaved "4 VMAT treatments plus 1 LRT per week" pattern. Sixteen spheres were placed within the gross tumor volume (GTV), achieving a peak-to-valley dose ratio (PVDR) of 3.52. Serial CT showed a reduction in the sum of lesion diameters (SOD) of 20.7% after eight VMAT fractions, 29.6% after 14 fractions, and 40% at the 2-month post-treatment assessment. The patient developed grade 4 hematologic toxicity and grade 1 radiation pneumonitis after additional systemic therapy.
CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates the delivery of weekly LRT during thoracic VMAT in a patient with bulky stage IIIB NSCLC, with significant tumor regression observed. This approach should be regarded as technically feasible in this case only, rather than as evidence that LRT can circumvent OAR (organs at risk) constraints or improve tumor control.

title: Using Unique Social Determinants of Health to Identify Patients at Risk of Not Receiving Lung Cancer Screening.
authors: Zollinger B, Dutra A, Ibrahim S et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sociodemographic barriers present one reason for low lung cancer screening (LCS) uptake. Our institution collects 13 unique social determinants of health (SDOH) via electronic health record. We sought to determine if specific SDOH factors are associated with LCS uptake.
METHODS: All LCS-eligible patients at our health system from January-May 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Unscreened patients without documented reason for not pursuing LCS were classified as "overdue". SDOH factors were collected along with demographic information. We compared these factors between screened and unscreened as well as screened and overdue.
RESULTS: 4389 LCS-eligible patients were reviewed with 1028 patients screened (23.4%) and 3370 patients unscreened (76.6%). Of the unscreened patients, 2332 (69.2%) were overdue. On univariate analysis of screened vs. overdue, 7 SDOH factors (social isolation, physical inactivity, food insecurity, financial strain, housing instability, transportation needs, and low health literacy) were significantly associated with a higher likelihood of no screening. On multivariable logistic regression using a composite score of the significant SDOH, registering one or more of the 7 identified SDOH risk factors was associated with higher likelihood of being unscreened (odds ratio [OR] 1.29; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.09-1.52) along with unemployment and family history of cancer. For screened vs. all unscreened, one or more SDOH risk factors of a composite of 6 (excluding social isolation) was similarly associated with no screening (OR 1.31; 95% CI 1.06-1.62).
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with one or more of seven unique SDOH risk factors may have a higher odds of missing LCS. Recognition of these risk factors may improve strategies to increase LCS uptake and mitigate sociodemographic disparity.

title: Dose-time-response relationships between radiation dose to the circulating blood and temporal changes in peripheral blood biomarkers during chemoradiation of non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Gaudreault M, Johnstone P, Chen A et al.
journal: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
abstract:
PURPOSE: Chemoradiotherapy commonly causes radiation-induced lymphopenia, neutropenia, and anemia, as measured by reductions in absolute lymphocyte count (ALC), absolute neutrophil count (ANC), and hemoglobin level (Hb). We aimed to quantify these hematological toxicities and characterize dose-time-response relationships between temporal changes in peripheral blood biomarkers and radiation exposure to the circulating blood during volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) definitive chemoradiotherapy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
METHODS AND MATERIALS: Blood biomarker measurements were collected from 93 NSCLC patients, treated between 2018 and 2024, at pre-, during-, and post-treatment time points. Radiotherapy prescription doses were 60 Gy in 30 fractions, 55 Gy in 20 fractions, or 50 Gy in 25 fractions with concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy. Organs at risks were delineated by the TotalSegmentator software. The blood dose-volume histogram was estimated through simulations of blood dynamics using the HEDOS software and VMAT dose accumulation was calculated with the BeamSplitter algorithm. Dose-time-response relationships were modelled by linear and exponentially decaying curves, from which rates of change were extracted and goodness of fit quantified using the R2- value.
RESULTS: Baseline blood biomarker values (median ± interquartile range) were (1.8±0.9) × 109/L for ALC, (5.6±3.0) × 109/L for ANC, and 132±19 g/L for Hb. Prior to treatment, 0%, 0%, and 30% of patients exhibited lymphopenia, neutropenia, and anemia, respectively. During treatment, these proportions increased to 71%, 19%, and 77%. Dose-response analysis revealed rates of change at low doses of radiation: -69%/Gy (ALC), -83%/Gy (ANC), and -3%/Gy (Hb), with model fits showing R² values between 0.78 and 0.96.
CONCLUSIONS: Hematological toxicities were frequent in NSCLC patients treated with VMAT chemoradiotherapy. Radiation exposure was associated with changes in circulating lymphocyte counts and hemoglobin, supporting prospective investigation into reducing circulating blood dose during chemoradiation to mitigate hematological toxicity.

title: Impact of Mental Health Disorders on Pulmonary Resection: A Society of Thoracic Surgeons General Thoracic Surgery Medicare Linked Study.
authors: Rosenbaum JJ, Bonnell LN, Parsons N et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To determine the prevalence of comorbid mental health disorders (MHDs) and association with stage of diagnosis, extent of resection, and post-operative morbidity/mortality in patients undergoing operative intervention for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
METHODS: Adults undergoing elective resection of stage I-III NSCLC were identified from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons General Thoracic Surgery Database (July 2018-June 2024) and linked to Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to determine long-term survival. Primary outcomes were stage at diagnosis, extent of resection, perioperative morbidity, and 5-year survival. Hierarchical multivariable logistic regressions estimated associations between MHDs on each outcome. Risk-adjusted survival was derived using multivariable frailty Cox proportional hazards regression.
RESULTS: Among 103,263 patients, 24.4% (n=25,163) had ≥1 MHD. Prevalence of MHDs increased from 16.8% in 2018 to 28.0% in 2024 (p<0.001). In risk-adjusted analysis, patients with an MHD were more likely to have clinical stage I disease (aOR 1.16, 95% CI 1.11-1.22) and to undergo sublobar resection (aOR 1.09, 95% CI 1.06-1.14). Perioperative mortality, morbidity, and length of stay were all significantly increased in patients with MHDs. In risk-adjusted analysis among Medicare linked patients, 5-year mortality was modestly but significantly greater among patients with MHDs (aHR 1.12, 95% CI 1.05-1.18).
CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of MHDs among patients undergoing NSCLC resection nearly doubled over 6 years and was associated with an ∼20% increase in morbidity and a reduction in adjusted 5-year survival. These findings underscore the need for targeted perioperative pathways and longitudinal support to mitigate adverse outcomes in this growing population.

title: Segmentectomy vs. Pulmonary Lobectomy in Resectable N1 NSCLC: The VESPER Study (VErification of Segmentectomy Versus Pulmonary Lobectomy in Resectable N1 Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer)
summary:
The VESPER study is an international, multicenter, retrospective cohort study designed to compare two surgical approaches-segmentectomy and lobectomy-for patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) who have pathologically confirmed N1 lymph node involvement after surgery. The study is sponsor-initiated and non-funded (spontaneous study), led by the Thoracic Surgery Unit of the IRCCS Azienda Ospedaliero-Universitaria di Bologna, Italy.

Traditionally, lobectomy has been considered the standard surgical treatment for patients with early-stage NSCLC, based on trials showing higher local recurrence rates after more conservative resections such as segmentectomy. However, more recent randomized studies (CALGB 140503 and JCOG0802/WJOG4607L) have shown that, in selected patients with small peripheral tumors (≤2 cm) and no lymph node metastases (clinical N0), sublobar resection-particularly segmentectomy-can achieve similar long-term survival and better preservation of lung function compared with lobectomy, though with a slightly higher local recurrence risk.

Despite these findings, there is still limited scientific evidence regarding the best surgical approach for patients with occult N1 disease (i.e., lymph node metastases discovered only after surgery). Some real-world and database studies suggest that completion lobectomy might not be necessary if a radical segmentectomy with an extended lymph node dissection is performed, but these results have not been validated in a large, multicenter cohort.

The VESPER study aims to fill this evidence gap by analyzing outcomes from nine participating centers. It will include approximately 400 patients who underwent pulmonary resection (segmentectomy, multisegmentectomy, or lobectomy) for pathologic N1 NSCLC between January 2018 and December 2021. About 50 patients are expected to come from the Bologna center.
